articles.title: Predicting Thermal Conductivity in Advanced BEOL Interconnect Stacks (Peking University)
articles.summary: Researchers at Peking University published a technical paper titled “Predictive Structure to Thermal Conductivity Modeling Framework for BEOL Interconnect Stacks in Advanced Technology Nodes Enabled by Extensive Layer Resolved Thermal Measurements.” Abstract Excerpt: “The increasing structural complexity of BEOL interconnect stacks in advanced integrated circuits demands a structure-aware thermal conductivity (κ) modeling framework. However, generalizable models derived from layer-resolved thermal measurements that quantitatively capture the dependence of κ on interconnect structures remain lacking, limiting predictive thermal analysis. Here, we establish an experimentally derived, structure-aware κ modeling framework enabled by time-domain thermoreflectance measurements with ~100 nm depth

articles.title: Agentic AI Automates Design-Rule Repair While Preserving Layout Equivalence (Purdue University)
articles.summary: Researchers at Purdue University published a technical paper titled “DRC-Aid: Design-Rule Correction via Agentic Framework utilizing Inference-Time Large Language Models.” Abstract Excerpt: “We present DRC-Aid, a closed-loop agentic framework that automates local DRC repair by formulating it as verification-in-the-loop search. To constrain the combinatorial geometric repair space, a deterministic Rule Engine converts physical verification tool-reported violations into a bounded menu of geometric edits. Find the technical paper here . July 2026. articles.title: Reinforcement Learning Cuts Routing Violations in Dense Chip Layouts  (NYU)
articles.summary: Researchers at New York University published a technical paper titled “Routing Dense Layouts with History-Aware Offline Reinforcement Learning using LSTM.” Abstract Excerpt: “Detailed routing remains a dominant runtime bottleneck in physical design due to increasing complexity of design rules. articles.title: Open Benchmark Evaluates AI Thermal Models for 2.5D and 3D ICs (UTS, TU Munich, ShanghaiTech)
articles.summary: Researchers at the University of Technology Sydney, ShanghaiTech University, and Technical University of Munich published a technical paper titled “IC-ThermBench: An Open, Progressive Benchmark for Generalizable 2.5D/3D-IC Thermal Learning.” Abstract Excerpt: “We introduce IC-ThermBench, an open and progressive benchmark that combines established 3D-IC steady-state, transient, and industrial package tasks with a new 50,000-sample 2.5D chiplet extension designed to evaluate progressively broader represented physical variation and cross-package OOD transfer. ” Find the technical paper here . August 2026. All apps, in order to take advantage of the larger inner display of iPhone Duo, will need to be recompiled for iOS 27.0 at a minimum. articles.title: I’ve tested dozens of wireless chargers — this is the first one I actually want to keep using
articles.summary: I’ve tested dozens of wireless chargers and desk setups over the years, and most of them suffer from the same problem. They all try to shoehorn everything into a single hub. There’s little, if any, flexibility in placement, choice of charging options, or future upgradeability. Moreover, as a design enthusiast, I care a lot about how a particular piece of tech looks in my space, and most chargers just aren’t very pretty to look at. But looks are subjective. Anyway, the fact is that most charging stations expect you to conform to a fixed layout for your phone, earbuds, and smartwatch . That’s fine for a functional product, but for one, the fixed layout has never really suited how I use my phone. Want to rearrange things? Tough luck.

articles.title: The iPhone 18 Pro isn’t worth $1,200, and the Pixel 11 Pro proves it
articles.summary: While the new iPhone Duo has received a lot of fanfare, the standard iPhone 18 Pro is going to be the one driving most of Apple’s sales. It doesn’t look much different from the iPhone 17 Pro on the outside, but Apple’s presentation was full of internal changes, from better battery performance to a new physically adjustable camera aperture. All those features do seem tempting at first glance, but I’d still go with the Pixel 11 Pro any day — just because it’s a much better overall purchase than its Apple counterpart.

articles.title: I use Google Maps every day, but Apple Maps still does these 4 things better
articles.summary: Be it a daily morning commute or a long road trip, most of us spend a surprising amount of time looking at Google Maps even without realizing it. Beyond the usual in-car navigation, it is my go-to when I’m looking for a new coffee shop or just checking transit schedules in a new country. And yet, lately, I find myself popping open Apple Maps more often than I expected. Apple has spent the last decade rebuilding Maps into a surprisingly capable navigation app. It might not beat Google Maps just yet, as Google still has the edge when it comes to local search and the sheer amount of information available. However, Apple has a few areas where its approach is simply better. Here are the things I prefer about Apple Maps and want Google Maps to copy.

articles.title: Your AI agent failed. The model might not be the problem.
articles.summary: As AI agents move into production, the path between a request and its result is becoming less predictable. An agent can choose its own tools and change course as it works, which makes failures harder to diagnose when there isn’t an obvious error to trace. In a recent interview with The New Stack , Nvidia VP of Product Adel el Hallak described the additional visibility developers will need as agents take on more complex work. Nvidia is also part of an industry effort to share what companies learn when those systems fail. articles.title: An undercover Google analyst infiltrated a notorious supply-chain hacking gang
articles.summary: Before two of its alleged members were arrested and charged in Australia last month, the hacker group known as TeamPCP carried out a hacking spree unlike any other in history. It tainted hundreds of open-source programs with its malware, stole developer accounts to perpetuate that software supply-chain hacking, and even released a Dune -themed self-spreading worm to automate the process, ultimately breaching more than a thousand companies. Now Google’s threat intelligence group has revealed that during a key moment of TeamPCP’s rampage, the company’s own undercover researcher had infiltrated the group—allowing Google to monitor the hacking spree from the inside, warn breach targets, and even help disrupt the group’s attempts to exploit those victims. articles.title: T. rex teeth indicate it ran as warm as an elephant
articles.summary: For most of the last century, T. rex was pictured as a sluggish, tail-dragging reptile that had to warm up in the sun before it could go anywhere. Then, further research changed that view, replacing it with the active, bird-like animal shown in the movie Jurassic Park . But whether T. rex used warm blood to power that activity remained a question. Now we might have gotten closer to an answer. A team of researchers led by Randon J. Flores and Robert A. Eagle, geochemists at the University of California, Los Angeles, has measured the T. rex body temperature by analyzing its teeth. This dental thermometer read about 36° Celsius—roughly the body temperature of a modern elephant.
